title: Gemma 4 on Amazon SageMaker: The NVIDIA T4 Decodes at 0.8x of the L4 With the Same Answers
why_read: A detailed, numbers-driven benchmark comparing GPU performance for serving a quantized LLM gives practical, verifiable guidance for cost-conscious ML deployment.
analysis: This article benchmarks running 4-bit quantized Gemma 4 models on a cheap NVIDIA T4 GPU on SageMaker versus a newer L4 GPU, measuring speed, memory use, and whether outputs stay identical across hardware. The core finding is that the older T4 runs at about 77-82% of the L4's decoding speed with the same quality, with a 12B model being the largest variant that fits in its memory, which is directly useful information for anyone choosing budget inference hardware. It also involves a specific technical fix, a 'Turing attention patch,' needed to get a modern inference engine like vLLM working on older Turing-architecture GPUs. This kind of concrete, reproducible hardware benchmarking is genuinely useful for engineers making GPU cost-performance tradeoffs.
